diagram_candidates.claim: For n ≥ 2, the B_n and C_n Dynkin diagrams have the same chain and a terminal double edge, with opposite arrow directions; transposing the Cartan matrix exchanges them.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The item is explicitly about diagram duality, and its verification calculates the terminal Cartan entries and their arrow conventions. A paired drawing would make the preserved chain and reversed arrow immediately visible.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Draw two n-node chains labeled α₁,…,αₙ for Bₙ and β₁,…,βₙ for Cₙ. Put the unique double edge between nodes n−1 and n in both; point the Bₙ arrow toward the short root αₙ and the Cₙ arrow toward the short root βₙ₋₁. Label the corresponding terminal Cartan entries (−1,−2) and (−2,−1), respectively, to show the transpose.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: The source calculations support both arrow directions and the Cartan-matrix transposition. This is an optional explanatory diagram; no existing diagram defect was found.
